appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Charlus naviguant vers nous de tout son corps énorme, traînant...un de ces apaches ou mendigots...ce monstre puissant...comme le requin par son pilote...contrastant tellement avec l'étranger hautain de la première année de Balbec; le vice jadis si intimement renfoncé par M. de Charlus...débordait maintenant dans ses propos.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator stages Charlus's dramatic physical and moral decline from the haughty stranger of early Balbec to a grotesque, bloated figure trailed by hangers-on, no longer able to conceal the vice he once hid so carefully.

appraisal_events.evidence: elle leur défendit de continuer à fréquenter M. de Charlus quand elle apprit que...il était comme fatalement amené, à chaque visite, à leur pincer le menton...les fils de Mme de Surgis s'éloignaient de M. de Charlus.
appraisal_events.explanation: Alarmed by Charlus's compulsive advances toward her sons, Mme de Surgis forbids them from continuing to see him, cutting off his access to their company.

appraisal_events.evidence: je me reprochais de ne pas avoir fait assez attention à lui...maintenant que je savais qu'il était comparable à l'un des plus beaux causeurs d'autrefois.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator retrospectively elevates Swann, regretting not having appreciated him enough now that he recognizes him as comparable to one of the great conversationalists of the past.

status_effects.explanation: Charlus is sharply diminished by the narrator's grotesque portrait of his physical and moral decay.
Charlus is cut off from the company of the Surgis sons by their mother's explicit prohibition, a clear boundary event.
Swann is somewhat elevated by the narrator's belated recognition of him as a remarkable conversationalist.
